name: tpl-precedence-2-goal
task: Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once. Reach the goal.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) makes key_lost forbidden until the door has first opened, but the task only forbids dropping the key while the door is closed. key_lost is false when the key is dropped after the door opens, so the clause does not capture the stated ban. Use a hard Absence(key_lost) for the ban; keep hard Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Absence(key_lost) forbids losing the key at any time, but the task only forbids dropping it while the door is closed until the door has been opened once. Replace it with hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost), which permits key_lost after the door has opened. Keep hard Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost) does not capture “do not drop the key while the door is closed.” key_lost is defined only for dropping the key while the door is closed, so the task’s wording calls for hard Absence(key_lost), not a ban that ends after the first opening. Keep hard Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: hard Absence(key_lost) bans every key_lost event, but the task only forbids dropping the key while the door is closed until it has been opened once. Replace it with hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost), which allows key_lost after the door has first opened. Keep hard Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: hard Absence(key_lost) forbids losing the key for the whole episode, but the task forbids dropping it only while the door is closed and until it has been opened once. Replace it with hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost), which permits key_lost after the door has been opened. Keep hard Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) does not match “Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once.” Because key_lost already means dropping the key while the door is closed, the task makes that ban Absence(key_lost), not a ban that ends after the first door opening. Replace the Precedence clause with hard Absence(key_lost); keep hard Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) is too broad. The task forbids dropping the key while the door is closed until it has been opened once; key_lost also covers dropping the key after the door has been opened and then closed again. Replace it with Absence(key_lost) and Precedence(door_open, key_lost), so drops are forbidden while the door remains closed but allowed after it has been opened.
NO CHANGES NEEDED: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) prevents losing the key while the door is still closed, and Existence(at_goal) requires reaching the goal.

texts: Do not lose the key before the door has been opened once.
